_note: v2 hook overrides for la Zone artisanale (B12_zone_artisanale). Source hooks are kept where the painting shows them; these replace hooks whose painted scene differs (no text, no weapons, varied animals), and three say lines are respelled so they never read as toilet words.

fr_service_noun.hook: "sehr-VEES" ≈ "SIR, VEE-S": a waiter in a black vest bows "SIR?" and carries in a tray of sandwiches: SERVICE.
fr_service_noun.why: He serves a tray of sandwiches, not tea.

fr_devoir_noun.hook: "duh-VWAHR": a schoolboy hugs a giant PENCIL beside his tall tower of HOMEWORK books: his DUTY, his homework.
fr_devoir_noun.why: No sword, not even a pencil one: the boy simply carries a giant pencil by his pile of books.

fr_travail_noun.hook: "trah-VAHY" ≈ "TRAVAIL": a young worker pushes a wheelbarrow across the yard with his TRAVEL case on top: WORK.
fr_travail_noun.why: A boy worker on flat ground instead of a man going uphill.

fr_industrie_noun.hook: "an-dews-TREE" ≈ "IN DUST TREE": through the window, tall factory chimneys puff DUST over the town: INDUSTRY.
fr_industrie_noun.why: The chimneys are seen through the window and are not tree-shaped.

fr_usine_noun.hook: "ew-ZEEN" ≈ "YOU SEEN?": a boy proudly holds up his model FACTORY with its tall chimney: "YOU SEEN my FACTORY?"
fr_usine_noun.why: He holds a model factory instead of pointing at real chimneys.

fr_brique_noun.hook: "BREEK" ≈ "BRICK": a boy in a work apron squeaks "BREEK!" and jumps away from the red BRICK he has just dropped.
fr_brique_noun.why: The dropped brick lies by his feet.

fr_assemblee_noun.hook: Like English ASSEMBLY — l'assemblée = the assembly, a gathering of people.
fr_assemblee_noun.why: They gather round a table indoors, under the bell, not in a yard.

fr_industriel_adj.why: A boy rather than a grown worker.

fr_site_noun.hook: "SEET" ≈ "SEAT": a boy sits on a folding SEAT in the big doorway, looking out over the empty building SITE.
fr_site_noun.why: He sits in the doorway rather than in the middle of the site.

fr_fabrique_noun.hook: "fah-BREEK" ≈ "FAB BRICK": a little FACTORY built of FAB red BRICKS stands on the workbench.
fr_fabrique_noun.why: The model is red brick and does not smoke.

fr_fabrication_noun.hook: Like English 'fabrication', said fah-bree-kah-SYOHN: a toy robot works a little press, MANUFACTURING parts.
fr_fabrication_noun.why: A press instead of a conveyor belt.

fr_concret_adj.hook: "kohn-KREH" ≈ "CONCRETE": a boy holds up his drawing of a house beside the real little houses on the bench: the plan becomes CONCRETE, real.
fr_concret_adj.why: The painting shows the boy with his drawing next to the real models, not a brick.

fr_chantier_noun.hook: "shahn-TYAY" ≈ "SHANTY": three little builders sing a sea SHANTY as they lift a wooden frame on the BUILDING SITE.
fr_chantier_noun.why: They lift a frame rather than lay bricks.

fr_producteur_noun.hook: "proh-DEWK-tuhr" ≈ "PRO DUCK TOUR": a proud hen PRODUCER stands by her crate of fresh eggs.
fr_producteur_noun.why: A hen instead of a duck, because rubber ducks already carry la production next door.

fr_beton_noun.hook: "bay-TOHN" ≈ "BAY TON": a pony peeps out of a BAY stall cast from a whole TON of gray CONCRETE.
fr_beton_noun.why: The pony stands in a concrete trough-stall.

fr_implantation_noun.hook: "an-PLAHN-tah" ≈ "IN PLANT": a girl waters a little model factory as if she had PLANTED it in the ground: SETTING UP a site.
fr_implantation_noun.why: A girl with a watering can instead of a giant hand.

fr_macon_noun.hook: "mah-SOHN" ≈ "MA'S SON": MA's SON, a young BRICKLAYER, leans over his long brick wall and trowels mortar along the top row.
fr_macon_noun.why: Only the son is painted: his MA lives in the sound, not the picture.

fr_montage_noun.hook: Looks like English "montage", but le montage mostly means ASSEMBLY: putting the parts together.
fr_montage_noun.why: A rocking horse instead of a bicycle frame.

fr_fabricant_noun.hook: "fah-bree-KAHN" ≈ "FABRIC CAN": a grandma MANUFACTURER rolls flowery FABRIC out of her clanking tin-CAN machine.
fr_fabricant_noun.why: A grandmother instead of an aunt.

fr_constructeur_noun.hook: Like English 'constructor', said kohns-trewk-TUHR: a young car CONSTRUCTOR tightens the last bolt on his shiny red model car.

fr_rendement_noun.hook: "RAHN-duh-MAHN" ≈ "RAN THE MAN": a man RAN his spoon machine so fast that a whole crate of wooden spoons pours out: OUTPUT, YIELD.
fr_rendement_noun.why: The painting shows the spoon-making machine and its pile of spoons.

fr_manufacture_noun.hook: Not the verb: une manufacture is a noun meaning a FACTORY, a workshop where things are made.
fr_manufacture_noun.why: A model factory with no visitors painted.

fr_productivite_noun.hook: Like English 'productivity', said proh-dewk-tee-vee-TAY: a busy beaver has already built a whole row of little chairs: such PRODUCTIVITY.
fr_productivite_noun.why: A beaver and its chairs instead of a four-armed worker; the clock beside it is just scenery.

fr_machiniste_noun.hook: Like English 'machinist', said mah-shee-NEEST: a young MACHINIST in a cap works at the little lathe.

fr_artisanat_noun.hook: "ahr-tee-zah-NAH" ≈ "ARTISAN, NAH!": a craftsman weaves a basket by hand: CRAFTS, handmade, NAH machines.
fr_artisanat_noun.why: A basket weaver instead of a potter, because the potter's vase is used next door for l'ouvrage.

fr_pourvoyeur_noun.hook: "pour-vwah-YUHR" ≈ "POUR, VOYAGER": a SUPPLIER with his pack has POURED grain into a fat sack for the VOYAGERS.
fr_pourvoyeur_noun.why: Respelled with "pour" so the sound line never reads as a toilet word.

fr_respiration_noun.hook: Like English 'respiration', said rehs-pih-rah-SYOHN: a girl throws her arms wide by the window and takes a deep BREATH of fresh air.
fr_respiration_noun.why: A girl at a window instead of a jogger by a turbine; the respelling avoids reading as a toilet word.

fr_poubelle_noun.hook: "pou-BEHL": a green BIN with a little brass BELL on its lid that rings each time trash goes in.
fr_poubelle_noun.why: Drops the old sound-alike, which read as a toilet word; the bell carries the -belle.

fr_ordure_noun.hook: "or-DEWR" ≈ "ORDURE": a fussy raccoon in an apron ORDERS a heap of GARBAGE into neat piles.
fr_ordure_noun.why: A raccoon instead of a crow, because a crow already carries le ravage upstairs. American words 2026-10-28: the meaning word in capitals changed to its American form (same painting).

fr_solaire_adj.hook: "soh-LEHR" ≈ "SO LAIR": a fox's LAIR roofed with a SOLAR panel, basking in the sun.
fr_solaire_adj.why: A fox instead of a cat.

fr_nucleaire_adj.hook: "new-KLAY-ehr" ≈ "NEW CLAY AIR": a boy shows his NEW CLAY model of an atom on its clay stand: NUCLEAR.
fr_nucleaire_adj.why: The model is an atom on a clay stand, with no cloud.

fr_charbon_noun.hook: "shahr-BOHN" ≈ "CHAR BONE": a little miner in a lamp helmet pushes his cart of black COAL, CHARRED like old BONES.
fr_charbon_noun.why: A miner boy pushes the cart.

fr_decharge_noun.hook: "day-SHAHRZH" ≈ "DAY CHARGE": the little dam opens its gates and lets out the water it held all DAY: a DISCHARGE, a RELEASE.
fr_decharge_noun.why: A dam releasing water instead of a battery spark, because la batterie is in the room.

fr_centrale_noun.hook: "sahn-TRAHL" ≈ "CENTRAL": a little model POWER PLANT stands at the CENTER of the control desk.
fr_centrale_noun.why: No trail of pylons is painted.

fr_polluant_adj.hook: "poh-LWAHN": a little red car puffs a gray cloud out of its exhaust: POLLUTING.

fr_conservation_noun.hook: Like English 'conservation', said kohn-sehr-vah-SYOHN: a ranger gently CONSERVES a little turtle beside the pond.
fr_conservation_noun.why: A turtle instead of a frog, because a frog lives in l'écosystème on the table.

fr_reacteur_noun.hook: "ray-ahk-TUHR" ≈ "RE-ACTOR": an ACTOR in a red cloak takes a bow beside the domed REACTOR model; also a jet ENGINE.
fr_reacteur_noun.why: The actor wears a stage cloak, not a lab coat (the lab coat is la contamination).

fr_rayonnement_noun.hook: "REH-yo-nuh-MAHN" ≈ "RAY-ON MAN": a boy glows with sunbeam RAYS, spreading light all round: RADIANCE.
fr_rayonnement_noun.why: A glowing boy instead of a man.

fr_ravage_noun.hook: Sounds like RAVEN + AGE, rah-VAHZH: in the painting on the wall a RAVEN flies over a field the storm has RAVAGED: flattened wheat, muddy torn furrows and an uprooted tree.
fr_ravage_noun.why: le ravage = devastation; the raven over the wrecked field

fr_climatisation_noun.hook: "KLEE-mah-TEE" ≈ "CLIMATE TEA": a little AIR CONDITIONER blows frost at a happy penguin: AIR CONDITIONING.
fr_climatisation_noun.why: A penguin instead of a cup of tea.

fr_ecolo_noun.hook: "ay-koh-LOH" ≈ "ECHO LOW": a young ENVIRONMENTALIST waters a sapling and waves a little leaf flag. (Informal, friendly.)
fr_ecolo_noun.why: He walks with a watering can instead of riding a bicycle, because the bicycle is le recyclage.

fr_recyclage_noun.hook: "ruh-SEE-klahzh" ≈ "RE-CYCLE": an old BICYCLE pieced together again from spare parts: RECYCLING.
fr_recyclage_noun.why: The bicycle is painted plain, so no tins or bottles are named.

fr_tentative_noun.hook: "tahn-tah-TEEV" ≈ "TENT TEEVEE": a small lopsided TENT on its first wobbly ATTEMPT to stand up.
fr_tentative_noun.why: No camper or TV manual is painted.

fr_consideration_noun.hook: Like English 'consideration', said kohn-see-day-rah-SYOHN: a woman holds the door with great CONSIDERATION for a boy pushing a stroller.
fr_consideration_noun.why: A woman holds the door for a boy, so it is not confused with l'égard below.

fr_ouvrage_noun.hook: "oo-VRAHZH" ≈ "OOH, VASE!": "OOH!" a grandma admires the blue vase she has just finished: a piece of WORK, handiwork.
fr_ouvrage_noun.why: One grandma admires her own vase.

fr_soutien_noun.hook: "soo-TYAN" ≈ "SUIT TIE-AN": a man in a SUIT and TIE props up the sagging roof beam with his arm: SUPPORT.
fr_soutien_noun.why: A roof beam instead of a ladder.

fr_egard_noun.hook: "ay-GAHR" ≈ "A GUARD": A GUARD walks an old lady and her shopping bag along with great CONSIDERATION.
fr_egard_noun.why: He escorts the old lady rather than holding a door (the door is la considération).

fr_reproche_noun.hook: "ruh-PROSH" ≈ "REPROACH": a teacher sitting on a big ROCK (roche) wags her finger: a REPROACH.

fr_appui_noun.hook: "ah-PWEE" ≈ "A PEW": a tired young man leans on a wooden post, checking his phone: SUPPORT, something to lean on.
fr_appui_noun.why: A post instead of a bench back.

fr_facilite_noun.hook: "fah-see-lee-TAY" ≈ "FAST, EASY TEA": toast pops up at the press of one button: EASE.

fr_routine_noun.hook: Sounds like roo-TEEN, ROO + TEEN: a teenage kangaroo in a hoodie and headphones checks off his morning checklist beside the alarm clock, the same ROUTINE every day.
fr_routine_noun.why: la routine = routine; roo + teen acted out by the teen kangaroo with his daily checklist

fr_paresse_noun.hook: "pah-REHS" ≈ "PA RESTS": a little one RESTS in a hammock, hands behind his head: LAZINESS.
fr_paresse_noun.why: A child in the hammock instead of Pa, and no lawn.

fr_prime_noun.hook: "PREEM" ≈ "PRIM": a PRIM manager in a suit hands a colleague a golden rosette: a BONUS, a PRIZE.
fr_prime_noun.why: A rosette instead of an envelope.

fr_efficacite_noun.hook: Like English 'efficacy', said ay-fee-kah-see-TAY: a clerk with six arms answers six phones at once: EFFICIENCY.
fr_efficacite_noun.why: Six arms are painted, not eight.

fr_moeurs_noun.hook: "MUHR" ≈ "MURR": two little figurines on a wall shelf: a gentleman doffs his top hat and a lady curtsies back: the polite CUSTOMS of the town.
fr_moeurs_noun.why: No cat is painted beside them.

fr_baril_noun.hook: Sounds like BARREL + REEL (bah-REEL): on the shelf a big fishing REEL is clamped to an oil BARREL, winding it in: le BARIL.
fr_baril_noun.why: le baril = barrel (of oil); the reel on the barrel acts out ba-REEL in the power plant.

fr_filiere_noun.hook: "fee-LYEHR": a young FILLY carries the fleece to the first child of the line: wool → yarn → knitting → sweater. la filière = the chain, the sector.

fr_rechauffement_noun.hook: "ray-shohf-MAHN": weatherman RAY's SHOW, MAN — he sweats, holding the thermometer and a map glowing red: global WARMING. le réchauffement = the warming.

fr_combustible_noun.hook: Looks like English "combustible" (it burns) — but in French it is a NOUN: le combustible = FUEL. The truck of logs is fuel.

fr_balayer_verb.hook: Up on tiptoe in a BALLET pose, Monsieur Verbe SWEEPS the cabin floor with his straw broom – BALLET, YAY! (bah-lay-YAY).
fr_balayer_verb.why: Un balai (a broom) → balayer = to sweep (je balaie la cuisine). RED beret = regular -er. (je balaie or balaye, nous balayons). Wave 1b oct30: moved from st_lavoir/balayeurs into zone_artisanale/cabane; hook rewritten to match the new painting.
